paragraphs.text: Read-only attachment library for DeepSeek Harness: every stored image and file, its size, and which
conversations still use it.
# dsh-plugin-attachment-library · Attachment library
English | 中文
A DeepSeek Harness (DSH) plugin that adds **Settings → Attachment library**: every image and file at
tachment stored on this machine, the space it takes, and which conversations still use it (active, a
rchived, moving to the trash, or in the trash).
**Read-only.** Nothing is deleted: the plugin never creates, changes, moves, or deletes an attachmen
t, a session log, a trash file, or a cache entry; "Show in Finder" only selects a file and never ope
ns or runs it. The plugin's only write is the read-only copy "Open in Preview" places in the system
temporary directory (outside DSH data), removed when the plugin stops. Its purpose is to check the r
eference counts before any cleanup is considered.

- DSH 0.2.x (`engines.dsh: >=0.2.0-rc.2 <0.3.0`, including the 0.2.1 alpha previews)
- Trash statist
ics work with `dsh-plugin-session-trash`; without it only existing conversations are counted
## Install
**Desktop**: open **Plugins** in the sidebar → **Add plugin**, enter one of the following, click **I
nstall**, then **Enable now** (new plugins start disabled):
- GitHub: `https://github.com/ZZZZZZZ-ZZZZZ/dsh-attachment-library`, or a version such as `github:ZZ

ZZZZZ-ZZZZZ/dsh-attachment-library#v0.4.1`
- npm: `dsh-plugin-attachment-library`
- An absolute path
to a local package, for example `/path/to/dsh-plugin-attachment-library-0.4.1.tgz` (made with `pnpm
ocal package, for example `/path/to/dsh-plugin-attachment-library-0.4.1.tgz` (made with `pnpm pack`)
Do not enter the source directory: its `node_modules` holds development copies of DSH packages that
conflict with DSH's own.
**Command line** (optional): quit DSH, then run `dsh plugin --profile desktop add dsh-plugin-attachm
e** (optional): quit DSH, then run `dsh plugin --profile desktop add dsh-plugin-attachment-library`.
**Uninstall**: uninstall "Attachment library" on the **Plugins** page. The plugin stores no data; at
tachments are not affected.
## What the page shows
- **Totals**: all attachments (count and size); images and files; used by existing conversations, us
ed only by conversations in the trash, and not used by any conversation (count and size each); attac

hments referenced but missing from the store; the size of the regenerable resize cache.
- **List**:
a type icon (an image icon for images, an icon by extension for files), type, file names (every name
stored for the same content), size, image dimensions and format, store time, and each referencing c
onversation with its title and status. An attachment shared by several conversations lists all of th

em.
- **Open in Preview** (macOS only): an arrow icon button on stored image rows (tooltip "Open in
Preview") opens the image in Preview on the Host. Preview gets a read-only copy with the right exten

sion, not DSH's own file (see below). File rows have no such button.
- **Show in Finder**: a folder
icon button at the right of each stored row (tooltip "Show in Finder") selects the file in the Host'
s Finder (Windows Explorer, or the default Linux file manager): a file attachment shows under its re
al file name, an image as its content-named object file. It appears only when the page talks to the
local DSH, the Host has a desktop file manager, and DSH allows desktop handoff; a failure is shown u

nder the row.
- **Rescan**: the refresh icon button at the top right (tooltip "Rescan"); it is disab

led while a scan runs, and "Rescanning…" is shown.
- **Filters**: type (all / images / files) and re
ferences (all / existing / trash only / unused); **sort** by time or by size (newest or largest firs

t). The list shows 100 rows at a time.
- **Incomplete logs**: session logs that could not be read in
full (damaged, cut short) are listed with a note that the "unused" counts may be too high.
## Why Finder shows no preview for images
DSH stores each image under its SHA-256 digest (for example `attachments/v1/objects/3f/3f9a…`) with
**no file extension**, read-only (0400). The content is an ordinary normalized JPEG, WebP, PNG, or G
IF, not encrypted; macOS decides the file type from the extension, so Finder shows no thumbnail and
a double-click does not open it as an image. File attachments differ: each also has a read-only hard
link under its real file name, which Finder shows normally.
## Counting rules
| Rule | Meaning |
| Identity | DSH stores attachments once per content digest (SHA-256); images and files are stored s

eparately, so the same bytes stored as an image and as a file are two rows |
| References | Every `{
type: 'image' \| 'file', attachment: { attachmentId } }` in a session log counts: user prompts, too

l results, and system messages |
| Conversations | A subagent session's references count for the con
versation that started it; a fork is its own conversation (it inherits its parent's prefix, so both

are listed) |
| Existing conversations | Every session the session backend lists, read through the o

fficial read-only handle; status active, archived, or moving to the trash |
| Trash | Logs inside th
e trash directory are read directly (raw JSONL or Zstandard frames); the title is the one recorded w

hen the conversation was moved |
[该节后续省略]
## Known limitations
- Images uploaded to the DeepSeek service (indexed in `<DSH home>/llm-deepseek/files-v3.json`) are n

ot counted and cannot be managed.
- Only the DSH 0.2.x attachment layout (v1) and the `dsh-plugin-se
ssion-trash` trash format (manifest version 1) are understood; a later major DSH version needs to be

checked again.
- Attachment contents are not re-hashed; only presence and size are used. Attachment

s referenced but missing are shown separately.
- Sessions the backend cannot read (written by a newe

r DSH, or damaged) add no references and are listed under "incomplete logs".
- One scan returns the

whole list; with tens of thousands of attachments the response is large and the first scan slow.
- W
hen Finder shows an attachment folder, Finder itself may write a `.DS_Store` (view state) file there

; that is Finder's behavior, and the plugin writes nothing.
- On Linux only the containing directory

opens; the file is not selected. The button is hidden when DSH is opened through remote access.
- "
Open in Preview" is macOS only. Copies stay until the plugin stops (or the system cleans its tempora

ry directory); after a DSH crash they may remain in the system temporary directory.
- Tested on macO
S only; the plugin only reads DSH data, so Linux and Windows are expected to work as well.
